Armor isn't about avoiding hits. Hits happen, that's the always-hit rule in action. Armor is what you wear and what you have been through: boiled leather, rings of steel, a breastplate that has already turned one blade. It is a choice about weight, slots, donning time, and what it says about you. What keeps you standing, though, is what you have trained. Damage Reduction comes from your talents, not from your gear.

Shields are different. A shield is not a passive number on your sheet, it is an active defense, something you put in the way of a blow. It gives you a reaction that downgrades an incoming hit. Wear your armor. Use your shield. Choose wisely.

#pagebreak()

== How Damage Reduction Works

When you take physical damage, subtract your Damage Reduction (DR) from the damage value. The remainder is what you actually lose from your HP. A hit always lands for at least 1 damage, no matter how much DR you have. Simple.

Your DR comes from talents such as Iron Skin (@sec-chapter-talents-abilities), not from your armor. What you wear can be boiled leather or full plate; the number that keeps you on your feet is the number you trained for.

*Example:* Kael has Iron Skin at Novice rank, so his DR is 2. A goblin's scimitar hits him for Weak damage (2). 2 - 2 = 0, but damage never drops below 1, so Kael takes 1 damage.

If the goblin lands a Standard hit (4 damage), Kael takes 2 HP. The same DR turns a solid hit into a scratch, whether Kael is wearing boiled leather or nothing at all.

#pagebreak()

What you wear is a choice about weight, donning time, and what it says about you, not about how much damage you stop.

#pagebreak()

== Shields

A shield is an active defense. You're not just wearing it, you're using it. When an attack comes in, you can throw the shield in its path.

The number before each shield is a Discipline requirement: you need that many ranks in the Protection Discipline to wield it, unless it came in your class starting kit (kit gear assumes training, see @sec-chapter-equipment). The full rules live in @sec-chapter-disciplines

*Buckler:* 1 Protection Discipline. Small, strapped to the forearm. Leaves your hand free for a second weapon or a wand.

*Shield:* 1 Protection Discipline. The standard. Wood and iron, carried in the off hand.

*Tower Shield:* 2 Protection Discipline, half cover. A portable wall. You move at -5 ft speed while carrying it. You can plant it as a maneuver to grant full cover to one ally directly behind you.

=== Shield Block (Reaction)

When you are hit by an attack, you may use your reaction to interpose your shield. Reduce the damage tier by one step: *Strong → Standard, Standard → Weak, Weak → 1 damage.* You must be wielding a shield and be aware of the attack. Reactions in general are covered in @sec-chapter-combat

Shield Block cannot reduce damage below 1. It can be used against melee attacks, ranged attacks, and spell attacks, anything you can see coming.

#quote[*DA Guidance:* Let the player declare Shield Block after hearing the damage tier result, not before. This makes shields feel active and tactical rather than just a passive DR bonus.]

#pagebreak()

== Worked Example: Choosing Your Armor

Roric is building a dwarf Protector at Level 1. He has Brawn +2, Fortitude +1, 13 HP, 1 Armor Discipline rank, and he has taken Iron Skin at Novice rank, so his DR is 2 whatever he wears. He wants to be the party's wall, but the wall has to fit inside a pack. Here's how he weighs his options:

*Leather:* Light, 2 slots, 1 minute to don. Cheap, quiet, and it leaves 2 slots of gear for the rest of his kit.

*Chain Mail:* Heavy, 4 slots, 10 minutes to don. It eats the slots he would rather spend on rope, a lantern, and a spare waterskin, and it takes ten minutes to get into.

Roric takes the leather and says so plainly: his DR is 2 either way. The chain mail would not make him harder to hurt, it would only make him heavier and slower to arm. He would rather carry the rope.

Armor is a decision about what the character can carry and how fast they can move, and his DR came from his training.

#pagebreak()

== Worked Example: Shield Block in Combat

Roric is holding a choke point against two goblins and their orc warchief. He's wearing the leather he chose above and carrying a shield, but the number that matters is on his character sheet: Iron Skin at Novice rank, so his DR is 2. The goblins aren't getting through easily.

Remember how this works. The DA never rolls for monsters (@sec-chapter-combat) The DA describes the attack and names the Challenge, and Roric's player makes the Defense Roll. Strong defense means the blow lands Weak, Standard means it lands Standard, Weak means it lands Strong. Roric has Parry rank 1 and a shield in hand, so he defends with 3d6 + Brawn + Parry rank - Challenge.

*Goblin 1 attacks:* "The goblin comes in low, scimitar slashing at Roric's shins. Challenge 1." Roric rolls 3d6 + Brawn +2 + Parry +1 - 1 = 3d6 + 2. He rolls 3, 4, 4 = 11 + 2 = 13. *Standard.* The scimitar's Standard damage is 4. DR 2 soaks 2, so Roric takes 2 damage. The blade dings off his shield with a sad _ping._

*Goblin 2 attacks:* "The second goblin circles wide, scimitar raised for an overhead cut. Challenge 1." Roric rolls 3d6 + 2. He rolls 1, 2, 3 = 6 + 2 = 8. *Weak.* The blow lands solid: Strong damage, 6. DR 2 soaks it to 4. Roric doesn't flinch. He's at 7 HP now, and he's only been standing here one round.

*Orc warchief attacks:* "The warchief says nothing. He doesn't need to. His greataxe comes around in a two-handed arc. Challenge 3." This is the one that matters. Roric rolls 3d6 + Brawn +2 + Parry +1 - 3 = 3d6. He rolls 4, 4, 3 = 11. *Standard.* The axe lands for Standard damage: 9.

*Roric's player:* "Shield Block."

He spends his reaction. The damage tier drops one step, Standard to Weak, and the incoming damage is now 6. DR 2 soaks 6 down to 4. The greataxe slams into Roric's shield, ringing off the boss like a temple bell. The haft cracks at the binding, but the blade never reaches him.

Without the block, Roric takes 9 - 2 = 7 damage, and at 7 HP that swing would have put him down. With it, he takes 4 and stays standing in the choke point. Shield Block is the shield's value now, because the DR comes from Iron Skin and not from the board in his hand.

#pagebreak()

== Donning & Doffing

Light armor (Padded, Leather, Studded Leather): 1 minute. Medium armor (Chain Shirt, Breastplate): 5 minutes. Heavy armor (Half Plate, Chain Mail, Plate): 10 minutes. Shield: 1 action.

You won't always have time to suit up. If the party is ambushed while camping, the Protector fights in whatever they were sleeping in. Plan accordingly: sleeping in chain mail is exactly as unpleasant as it sounds.

#callout(type: "note", title: "Armor Isn't the Point", body: [
Your DR is a small, fixed number from a talent like Iron Skin. It will not save you from a bad position, and it will not save you from five goblins. Five goblins all attacking the same target will eventually wear down even the toughest Protector through sheer volume of hits.

Use cover. Use positioning. Use the fact that you're harder to kill than everyone else to _control where the fight happens._ The Protector's real armor isn't steel, it's standing in the right place at the right time.
])
